integrity: The proof starts from the motivating article's printed equilibrium quadratic. Once the bird equilibrium is positive, its constant term is strictly negative, which forces exactly one positive human root. The source-specific formula and three small-spillover asymptotics are independently checked by the bundled standard-library script.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns existence and asymptotic response of the all-positive equilibrium, not its local or global stability.
Positive bird-to-human transmission is essential; when it is zero, the autonomous human threshold is recovered.
The closed root formula assumes positive human-to-human transmission; the zero-transmission case is a separate linear limit.
The result does not claim novelty for the general epidemiological idea that recurrent reservoir spillover can sustain subcritical human infection.
title: Reservoir spillover removes the human endemic threshold in a coupled avian-influenza model
